guide.title: AED & Defibrillation
guide.lead: Every minute without a shock in VF lowers survival. Get the pads on fast, keep compressing while the AED gets ready, and go straight back to compressions after the shock. Don't check the pulse after a shock.

steps.title: Power on
steps.text: Keep compressions going while your partner prepares the pads.

steps.title: Pads on bare, dry chest
steps.text: Anterolateral (right upper chest below the clavicle; left side in the mid-axillary line) or anteroposterior.

steps.title: Compress immediately
steps.text: For 2 minutes before the next analysis. No pulse or rhythm check right after the shock.

sections.title: Pad problems
rows: Shave, or rip off a first set of pads
Dry the chest; move out of standing water
Remove it and wipe the skin
Don't place a pad directly over it
Press firmly, dry, shave or replace pads
Keep the source away from the chest during the shock

sections.title: Energy
rows: Per manufacturer (typically 120–200 J); 200 J if unknown
First 2 J/kg, second 4 J/kg, then 4 J/kg or more (max 10 J/kg or adult dose)
notes: Under 8 years: pediatric pads or attenuator if available, otherwise a standard AED.
Infants: manual defibrillator preferred, then attenuated AED, then standard AED.
If pads could touch on a small chest, use anteroposterior.

quiz.q: The AED has just delivered a shock. What next?
quiz.explanation: 2 minutes of CPR before the next analysis.

quiz.q: A 6-year-old in arrest; only adult pads, no attenuator. You should:
options: Use the adult pads, anteroposterior so they don't touch
Use anterolateral pads, overlapping is fine
quiz.explanation: A shock is better than no shock.

quiz.q: "Check electrodes" keeps appearing; the chest is very hairy. Best action?
options: Remove the pads, shave, apply new pads firmly
Press on the pads with your hands during analysis
quiz.explanation: Never touch the patient during analysis.
Asystole and PEA need CPR and epinephrine.

quiz.q: Biphasic energy when the manufacturer's dose is unknown:
First shock dose for a child:
A nitroglycerin patch sits where the pad goes. You should:
options: Remove it and wipe the skin before applying the pad
Move the pad to the abdomen
quiz.explanation: Patches can burn and block energy.

quiz.q: A bulge under the left clavicle (pacemaker). Pad placement?
Patient in arrest lying in a puddle:
options: Move out of the water and dry the chest before the shock
Don't use an AED in the rain
quiz.explanation: A dry chest and no standing water protect rescuers and the shock.

options: An adult AED with pads overlapping
quiz.explanation: Then an attenuated AED, then a standard AED.

flashcards.question: AED in 4 steps
flashcards.answer: Power on; pads on bare chest; analyse (hands off); shock if advised, then CPR at once.

flashcards.question: Anterolateral pad placement
flashcards.answer: Right upper chest below the clavicle; left side of the chest in the mid-axillary line.

flashcards.question: Shockable rhythms
flashcards.answer: VF and pulseless VT. Asystole and PEA are not shockable.

flashcards.question: Safety before a shock
flashcards.answer: Look and shout "clear"; oxygen away from the chest; remove patches; dry chest; pads well stuck and not touching.

flashcards.question: Pediatric pads
flashcards.answer: Under 8 years: pediatric pads or attenuator. None available: standard AED, pads anteroposterior if they'd touch. A lone rescuer with an unwitnessed collapse gives about 2 minutes of CPR before fetching the AED.

flashcards.question: Right after a shock
flashcards.answer: Compressions immediately for 2 minutes. No pulse or rhythm check.

flashcards.question: Adult energy
flashcards.answer: Biphasic per manufacturer (typically 120–200 J; 200 J if unknown). Monophasic 360 J.

flashcards.question: Child energy
flashcards.answer: First 2 J/kg, second 4 J/kg, later 4 J/kg or more (max 10 J/kg or adult dose).

critical.scenario: The mall AED shocked once and prompted CPR. 30 seconds into compressions, your monitor through the pads shows fine VF. Your partner asks whether to shock again.
critical.question: Shock now or continue CPR?

options.t: Continue CPR for the full 2 minutes, then re-analyse
options.f: Correct. The waveform during compressions is artefact-prone and the heart needs perfusion.
Stacked shocks interrupt perfusion; finish the cycle.

options.t: Stop CPR to look at the rhythm

critical.explanation: Keep pre- and post-shock pauses short.

critical.scenario: A sweaty 68-year-old in arrest. The pads keep sliding off even after drying; the AED says "Check electrodes – poor contact".
critical.question: How do you fix it?

options.t: Dry again, apply a fresh set of pads, press firmly especially at the edges; switch to the manual defibrillator's pads if needed
Ignore the warning: it'll shock anyway
options.f: High impedance can stop the shock and cause burns.

options.t: Hold the pads on during analysis
options.f: Never touch the patient during analysis or a shock.
Fix the contact; keep compressing meanwhile.

critical.explanation: Good contact is needed for the AED to analyse and for an effective shock.

critical.scenario: A man collapsed at a bus stop in heavy rain. He's lying in a puddle, pulseless, with a bump under the left clavicle.
critical.question: How do you prepare the shock?

options.t: Move him out of the water, dry the chest, place the pads away from the device (anteroposterior works)

options.f: Standing water is a hazard; move first.
It blocks energy and can damage the device.

options.t: No AED because of the pacemaker

critical.explanation: Keep compressions going during preparation; pause only to analyse and shock.
critical.kpi: Prepares safe defibrillation in a wet environment with an implanted device
